enhanced_information: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is caused by an imbalance of normal vaginal flora, primarily involving a decrease in Lactobacillus species and an overgrowth of other bacteria. The first-line treatments for BV are antibiotics, with metronidazole and clindamycin being the most commonly recommended options. Clinical guidelines consistently support metronidazole as a first-line treatment due to its proven efficacy in clinical studies. Clindamycin is also effective and recommended, but metronidazole is generally preferred. Erythromycin and ampicillin are not recommended as first-line treatments for BV, as clinical evidence does not support their use for this condition. Therefore, the best treatment options are metronidazole and clindamycin, with metronidazole being the most established first-line choice.
